newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk sell-off adviser fears Telekom law annulment.
newsitem.headline: Turk sell-off adviser fears Telekom law annulment.

text.p: A legal adviser to Turkey's privatisation authorities said on Thursday he feared the constitutional court would next week annul a law designed to enable the sale of Turk Telekom.
"Law number 4161 will be annulled on January 21. You don't need to be a soothsayer (to predict that)," said Yahya Zabunoglu, a legal adviser to the Privatisation Administration (OIB).
But he went on to qualify his statement.

"But this is Turkey. What will happen is not certain. I am not speaking in the name of the OIB, I am a paid adviser. God willing what I have said will not happen," he said at a privatisation discussion meeting.
The constitutional court, which is expected to announce a ruling on the law next Tuesday, annulled a previous draft, Zabunoglu noted.
A group of 116 mainly leftist deputies made the latest annulment application to the court last August.

State telecommunications company Turk Telekom is the centrepiece of the government's sell-off programme and progress in pushing ahead with its privatisation in 1997 is vital to the government's plans.
State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said earlier Turkey would prepare at least $750-$800 million worth of sell-offs during January.
"This month privatisations worth at least $750-$800 million will be made ready to be presented to the OYK (High Board of Privatisation)," Soylemez said at a discussion meeting.
He added that if conditions were right the total could be as high as $1 billion.
